subject.title: Bundled plugin loader rejects hardlinked files (nlink > 1) — breaks plugin loading on NixOS with auto-optimise-store

question: Should canonical bundled public artifacts under the resolved OpenClaw package or bundled-plugin root be exempt from final-file hardlink rejection, matching the existing facade-loader boundary behavior?
rationale: The observable bug has a narrow likely repair, but the generic hardlink guard was introduced as security hardening; maintainers need to confirm that the exception is limited to OpenClaw-owned bundle roots and does not become a general plugin-root bypass.

options.title: Approve a narrow bundled-root exception
options.body: Set this public-artifact call path to accept hardlinks only after canonical bundled-root resolution, while retaining realpath containment, inode identity revalidation, and focused hardlink coverage.

options.title: Keep rejection and provide a supported Nix packaging path
options.body: Retain the strict loader behavior and document or implement a packaging mechanism that materializes bundled runtime artifacts without hardlinks.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow bundled-root exception
recommendation.body: Set this public-artifact call path to accept hardlinks only after canonical bundled-root resolution, while retaining realpath containment, inode identity revalidation, and focused hardlink coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: Current project direction explicitly balances safe defaults with stability and setup reliability; this is a security-boundary compatibility choice.
